#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

DEST='backup-srv:/srv/nightly'
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/
scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST/"

arguments.command:
set -eu
ls -l backup.sh
command -v shellcheck >/dev/null 2>&1 && shellcheck backup.sh || true
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$tmp/logs" "$tmp/bin"
printf 'sample\n' > "$tmp/logs/app.log"
cp backup.sh "$tmp/backup.sh"
cat > "$tmp/bin/tar" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = -czf ] && [ "$3" = logs/ ]
printf 'archive' > "$2"
EOF
cat > "$tmp/bin/scp" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz" ]
[ "$2" = backup-srv:/srv/nightly/ ]
EOF
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/tar" "$tmp/bin/scp"
(
  cd "$tmp"
  PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" ./backup.sh
  test -f "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz"
)
printf 'backup.sh isolated smoke test passed\n'
